facts.fact: A Thurai herald asks the queen for a three-day truce at the stakes; Kandan counts about forty red-crested officers' caps among the dead, and the host withdrew to the beach under sergeants.
facts.why: needed because the outline opens with the Thurai withdrawing short of captains and asking a truce

facts.fact: The queen never read any of Chathu's forty pages at night; she watched him write them over four evenings and did not wish to test a leaf on a stranger. Neela finds them dry-inked and without resin smell.
facts.why: needed because the plain-ink discovery requires the pages to be untested

facts.fact: Chathu's tin of warm sweets and the note 'Written off. Paid in full. C.' in common grey-brown ink reach Neela by the palace post with the column's last rider, handed over by a steward of the queen's household.
facts.why: needed because the outline has the queen's post bring the tin and note

facts.fact: Neela has checked every village on the thirty crown-leaf intake rolls against Devan's border roll of raids and finds each was raided in the year its child was taken.
facts.why: needed because the outline has the intake villages matching the raids
